recommendations: 1. Etsy: $16.99 with free shipping per keychain (or $12.99 + $5.99 shipping); 3 for $39.99; custom body colour +$2.
2. Car meets / in person: $10 each or 3 for $25. Bring a mix of the 9 cars in black/white plus a few popular colours.
3. Car clubs (10+ of one car, club colour): $9 each. Wholesale to shops (20+): $7 each (they retail at ~$15).
4. Print the 1-swap PLATE files for stock. Keychains cost ~$0.25-0.35 in materials + printer time; your time and shipping are the real costs.
5. Bundle to spread the ~$6 shipping label: a 3-pack earns far more per keychain than three single orders.
6. Custom colours: printed as smaller batches (8 filament changes per plate); the +$2 covers the extra purge and printer time.
7. Brand logos and names (BMW, Porsche, Mercedes, Ford/Shelby, Chevrolet, Audi, Lamborghini) are trademarks. Selling them risks takedowns on Etsy/eBay.
Lower-risk option: sell badge-free versions (set badge_on=False / SHOW_BADGE=False and rebuild) and describe cars generically, not with brand logos.
8. Re-check your numbers every few months: filament deals, USPS prices and Etsy fees change. Edit the blue cells on Inputs.

sources.item: CORRECTION: filament wasted on colour changes (K2 CFS)
sources.finding: The stock firmware purges a fixed ~100 mm on every CFS swap, which I calculate at about 0.30 g (from 1.75 mm diameter and 1.24 g/cm3 PLA). The slicer's flush comes on top of that. One user reported a small 4-colour model with 309 colour changes using 18x more filament than the model itself. A K2 guide estimates 30-40% waste on 4-colour prints with frequent changes. Purge waste per plate does not grow with the number of copies on the plate, so batching reduces waste per keychain. Model input (estimate, low confidence): about 1-3 g per keychain when printing 8-12 per plate, about 5-15 g for a si
(8-15 g part + 1-3 g purge share) x $0.020/g = about $0.18-0.36; typical 10 g x $0.02 = $0.20. Add about 10% for failed prints. A one-off custom single keychain: about $0.30-0.60.
K2 Combo with CFS $549 (store shows it as reduced from $699). K2 without CFS $399 (from $549). October 2025 reviews quoted $799 for the Combo, which is out of date.

sources.item: Printer wear cost per hour (depreciation + maintenance)
sources.finding: $549 over about 5,000 print hours = $0.11/h, plus about $0.03/h for nozzle and plate wear. Prusa's own rates run $0.10-0.36/h.

sources.item: K2 average power draw printing PLA
sources.finding: No measured figure exists for the base K2. Confirmed specs: 70 W rated hotend, 100 C max bed, no chamber heater. The K1 measured about 100 W average while printing (370 W peak while heating, 20 W idle). Estimate 100-150 W; use 0.13 kW.
18.31 cents/kWh in July 2026 (17.45 cents in July 2025). At 0.13 kW that is about $0.024 per printer-hour, which is negligible.

Prusa's method counts about 5-10 minutes of handling per job. For a keychain (plate removal, cleanup, attaching the ring, packing, messages) use about 6 min at $15-20/h = $1.50-2.00. At low prices this costs more than all the materials combined.
